title: Why NVIDIA Wants TSMC 3nm at the Base of Its Next-Generation HBM
gist: NVIDIA is reportedly pushing Samsung, SK hynix and Micron to build the logic base dies of its custom next-gen HBM (NVHBM) on TSMC 3nm for a common foundation across suppliers; Samsung reportedly agreed despite its own foundry. The post argues NVIDIA's influence now reaches deep into supplier process choices and memory differentiation is shifting toward logic design.

insights.claim: NVIDIA is reportedly pushing Samsung Semiconductor, SK hynix and Micron Technology to use TSMC's 3nm process for the base dies of its next-generation custom high bandwidth memory, NVHBM.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Adds a new high-value leading-edge wafer demand stream for TSMC from the HBM supply chain.

insights.claim: The 3nm requirement for NVIDIA's custom HBM applies only to the logic base die beneath the stack; the stacked DRAM dies continue to use specialized DRAM processes.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Clarifies that the shift benefits logic foundry capacity, not DRAM process economics.
insights.quote: this does not mean the entire memory stack moves to 3nm

insights.claim: According to Seoul Economic Daily, NVIDIA wants a common manufacturing foundation across its three HBM suppliers to improve consistency and reduce the effort to validate different implementations.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: NVIDIA is standardizing suppliers to cut qualification cost, increasing its leverage over memory vendors.

insights.claim: A shared base-die process could simplify NVIDIA's supplier qualification and platform integration, though it does not prove that different suppliers' finished HBM products become interchangeable.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: If HBM drifts toward interchangeability, memory vendors' pricing power could erode.

insights.claim: Samsung reportedly accepted NVIDIA's request to use TSMC for the custom HBM base die, though this is reported industry information rather than a jointly announced production agreement.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: A Samsung memory win built on TSMC logic is a negative signal for Samsung Foundry's captive volume.

insights.claim: Samsung using TSMC for an NVIDIA custom product would show customer requirements outweighing its integrated memory-plus-foundry approach and traditional competitive boundaries.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Undercuts the thesis that Samsung's vertical integration is an HBM advantage.
insights.quote: Using TSMC for NVIDIA’s custom product would show how customer requirements can outweigh traditional competitive boundaries.

insights.claim: SK hynix previously said that adopting TSMC's advanced logic for HBM base dies would enable more functionality in limited space and support customization for performance and power efficiency.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: SK hynix's existing TSMC alignment gives it a head start on custom HBM.

insights.claim: TSMC would gain a new role in the AI supply chain, extending beyond accelerator manufacturing into customized memory logic.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Expands TSMC's AI-related TAM into HBM logic dies.
insights.quote: TSMC would gain another role in the AI supply chain, extending beyond accelerator manufacturing into customized memory logic.

insights.claim: AI performance increasingly depends on coordinated development across compute, memory and packaging, with memory differentiation increasingly involving logic design alongside DRAM density and bandwidth.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Memory makers' competitive edge shifts toward logic-design capability and foundry partnerships.
insights.quote: memory differentiation increasingly involves logic design alongside DRAM density and bandwidth

insights.claim: NVIDIA's influence now reaches deep into its suppliers' technology choices, including which foundry builds memory base dies.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Highlights NVIDIA's bargaining power over the memory supply chain.
insights.quote: NVIDIA’s influence now reaches deep into its suppliers’ technology choices
